enforcement.agentContainer: internal-only run network; reachable endpoints: gateway:8811 (Bearer auth) and llm-proxy:3128 (CONNECT allowlist: api.anthropic.com:443); no workspace, output, or docker-socket mounts; model API key present by necessity
enforcement.exec: no exec: run_command tool not exposed; harness built-in shell toolsets never enabled
enforcement.filesystem: read none; write none — enforced by the tools-container mount table (ro/rw, per-path binds) plus server-side grant checks; on Linux the run's docker filter mounts the tools container's /tmp as a 256 MiB tmpfs and the tools server refuses to serve without it; under Docker Desktop (macOS, Windows), which runs no filter, it is the container's own layer, unbounded
enforcement.model.apiKey: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the host environment, injected into the agent container (or the host harness process) only
enforcement.network: no egress: tools container runs with networking disabled (disableNetwork); no fetch tool exposed
enforcement.pdf: the runner's grant, not the contract's: export_pdf renders a Markdown file from reports/ or the scratch folder into a PDF in reports/ with Typst 0.15.1 in the tools container (built without a package downloader), through the runner's confine role: an empty environment, a fresh render root under /tmp whose every file the tools server makes new, no write of its own (Landlock; the PDF comes back on its stdout), TCP refused where Landlock is ABI 4 or later, 1 GiB of address space and 60 seconds; as root it runs as a user of its own that owns nothing, and where there is no Landlock that user is all that holds its writes. Only local PNG and JPEG images from reports/, the scratch folder and the inputs are drawn. The theme is the run's, never the model's, and the receipt's pdfs block names it and each PDF's SHA-256; write_report refuses a PDF
enforcement.scratch: the runner's grant, not the contract's: scratch_list, scratch_read and scratch_write over the scratch folder /scratch on the tools container only, empty at the start, never copied to the output folder, and removed with the container; on Linux a 256 MiB tmpfs the run's docker filter mounts, under Docker Desktop a folder in the container's own layer, unbounded
